decisions.reason: The scenario review of the factory-face proposal says width and height are the face estimate_pose_chamfer_v3_2 already matches, params.pallet_width_m 1.20 m and params.pallet_height_m 0.14 m, and that a successful estimate can still reach the handling process with that face and no body depth. It says the scenario states no rule that a missing body is a flag, and no rule that the median far-side length through the two fork openings is the pallet depth. A sample_face_points return inside a pocket can be the pallet body, a load, the floor, or another object, and that median is what the handling process would read as depth. The scenario review of the silhouette proposal under the same id says the scenario states no rule that an inlier span past the factory 1.20 m by 0.14 m face is a larger pallet, so the handling process would size the approach from structure the chamfer match did not use, while a short silhouette is still published as the factory face and the pocket median has the same gap. The feasibility review says the package has no filled pocket rectangle and no point-in-rectangle test, the inverse map that places those samples in prototype coordinates has no caller, and the chamfer translation is dropped on return, so publish_pose cannot form the silhouette. Stage 2 still estimates the one candidate select_detection already chooses, and which detections are deferred stays off the message. The proposals do not restate dimension_error_m or latency_ms, and this id is not already kept or rejected.

The scenario review says the handling process uses which detected pallets are sent through stage 2 versus marked deferred while the scene can still change. published_admission_split ranks this capture's class-matched DetectionCandidate list with the strategy select_detection already implements, keeps the earlier candidate on a tie by the first-maximum rule std::max_element already uses, admits the one pallet the pose node asks to pose, and writes that source index together with the deferred source indices on PalletPoseStamped after input_depth_stamp. The message already carries this pair's RGB and depth stamps, so both sides of the named split sit on the pose result for this capture. The user named the split. The part they did not name is that the split is these two admission vectors, in that order, on that pose result. The rejected stage2_subset_admission left the vectors with the caller. This proposal writes them on the pose result, and when the estimate fails it writes them on the failure diagnostic, the only result that path publishes. The scenario states no rule that a failed estimate must still publish PalletPoseStamped, and a count of one is the one pallet the scenario asks for. The feasibility review says that count with the same first-maximum rule matches today's winner, source_index is the array slot extract_detection_candidates already stored, and the deferred indices stay in the local candidate list until the publishers receive the split. PalletPoseStamped still ends at input_depth_stamp, the failure diagnostic has to carry the lists as text, the geometry_msgs pose on the same path has no custom fields, and the recorder copies neither list. The empty-candidate return and the depth-image throw still publish nothing. Those limits leave the named split on PalletPoseStamped for a successful estimate and on the failure diagnostic when the estimate fails. The proposal does not restate dimension_error_m or latency_ms, and it is not already kept or rejected.
